0.0.n: This noun identifies what the anniversary celebrates.

0.1.n: 周年 counts years since something began; 30周年 marks thirty years.

0.2.n: After an anniversary expression, this noun announces a celebration marking the occasion.

0.4.n: This describes successive entries in the movie series, not just one older film.

0.5.n: This is the first part of ブルーレイ, a single borrowed word split here by the app.

0.6.n: This completes ブルーレイ, the disc format; it is not used independently here.

0.7.n: が marks the Blu-ray releases as what the announcement is about.

0.8.n: This noun refers to products going on sale, rather than films opening in theaters.

0.9.n: だ is the casual equivalent of です, turning 発売 into an announcement.

0.10.n: ゾ is a playful katakana spelling of ぞ, adding forceful, excited emphasis.

1.0.n: 懐かしい expresses fond feelings about the past; です makes the remark polite.

1.1.n: This ending draws out the speaker’s reflective feeling, as if savoring a memory.

2.0.n: この must come before a noun; here it points to the period being shown.

2.1.n: 頃 refers to an approximate period rather than an exact moment.

2.2.n: の links この頃 to オラ, identifying the speaker’s younger self from that period.

2.3.n: オラ is a rustic, highly casual form of I, used here as the character’s distinctive self-reference.

2.5.n: This softens the description and makes the question sound casual.

2.6.n: 幼い becomes 幼くない in the negative; rising question intonation invites agreement that the speaker looks young.

3.0.n: This duration tells how long the release schedule will take.

3.1.n: The て-form of かける links the time spent to the release action that follows.

3.2.n: 発売する becomes 発売して, then adds いく to show releases continuing forward over time.

3.3.n: ゾ gives the announcement a spirited, emphatic finish and matches the character’s playful speech.

0.lit: Movies’ 30th-anniversary commemoration! Blu-rays from across the years are going on sale!
0.tip: 発売だ is a punchy announcement of a release; it does not by itself specify an exact release date.

1.tip: ですなぁ combines politeness with a drawn-out, reflective ending, giving the remark a somewhat old-fashioned flavor.

2.lit: The me of this time, isn't he a little young?
2.tip: A negative adjective question like 幼くない？ often asks for agreement: Don't I look young?

3.lit: Taking one year, they will go on releasing them!
3.tip: ていく shows the releases unfolding over time, rather than happening all at once.
